nodes.description: Private uint256 holding the secret number between 1 and 16; written by shuffle() and read by play() to decide the winner.
Public uint256 timestamp of the last play; written in play() with now and read by kill() for the 6 hour time lock.
Public uint256 minimum bet of 0.2 ether validated by the require() in play().
Public address of the owner, initialized to msg.sender in the constructor and used as the authorization check in kill().
Public Game[] array recording every player address and guessed number via push().
CryptoRoulette constructor: sets ownerAddr = msg.sender and calls shuffle() to initialize secretNumber.
Internal function that derives secretNumber from sha3(now, block.blockhash(block.number-1)) % 16 + 1.
Payable game entry point: validates value and guess, records the Game, pays the caller the whole balance on a win, then reshuffles and updates lastPlayed.
Privileged function that selfdestructs and sends the balance to the owner only if msg.sender == ownerAddr and now > lastPlayed + 6 hours.
Payable fallback function that accepts plain ether transfers into the contract.
Attacker-controlled caller address used as game player, transfer recipient, suicide beneficiary and owner comparison.
Miner-influenced 'now' value used both as randomness entropy in shuffle() and as the time-lock base in kill().
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) executed inside play() before the state is refreshed, an external value call that can re-enter the contract.
suicide(msg.sender) inside kill(), an irreversible selfdestruct that pays the caller, guarded only by an address and timestamp check.
sha3(now, block.blockhash(block.number-1)) % 16 + 1, a predictable on-chain pseudo-randomness computation that determines secretNumber.
User-supplied uint256 'number' argument of play(), validated as <= 16 and compared to secretNumber.
Temporary Game struct built inside play() holding player = msg.sender and number before being pushed to gamesPlayed.

edges.reason: Constructor assigns ownerAddr = msg.sender, linking the untrusted caller to the owner state variable.
play() writes game.player = msg.sender, storing the untrusted caller in the local Game struct.
The untrusted msg.sender is both the trigger and the beneficiary of msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) in play().
kill() is gated by the comparison msg.sender == ownerAddr, an authorization check on untrusted caller data.
suicide(msg.sender) forwards the entire balance to the caller, authorized only by the owner/timestamp checks in kill().
kill() conditionally invokes the selfdestruct operation after passing the owner and 6 hour time-lock checks.
The miner-influenced now value is consumed as entropy by the sha3-based secretNumber computation, a timestamp dependency.
play() writes lastPlayed = now, making a state variable dependent on the miner-influenced timestamp.
kill() uses now > lastPlayed + 6 hours, a timestamp-dependent authorization condition.
The constructor invokes shuffle() to initialize secretNumber.
play() calls shuffle() after each attempt to pick a new secretNumber.
play() performs the external value transfer before calling shuffle() and updating lastPlayed, so state is stale during the transfer.
transfer() to msg.sender can invoke the recipient's payable fallback function while play() is still executing.
The external transfer can re-enter play() before secretNumber and lastPlayed are refreshed, enabling repeated payouts.
shuffle() assigns the derived value to the secretNumber state variable.
The output of the predictable sha3/timestamp randomness expression becomes secretNumber.
play() reads secretNumber in the comparison number == secretNumber to decide the winner.
play() requires msg.value >= betPrice, reading the betPrice state variable.
play() writes lastPlayed from the timestamp at the end of the call.
play() constructs the local Game struct for the current player.
The number parameter is stored into game.number before the struct is persisted.
gamesPlayed.push(game) persists the local Game struct into the gamesPlayed array.
kill() reads ownerAddr to compare it against msg.sender before selfdestructing.
kill() reads lastPlayed to enforce the now > lastPlayed + 6 hours condition.

normalization_plan.reason: The user-supplied 'number' parameter only exists as the input of play(), where it is range-checked and compared with secretNumber, so it is folded into the play() node.
The 'game' struct is a short-lived local created inside play() and immediately pushed to gamesPlayed, so it is folded into the play() node.
